question.prompt: What is the x-coordinate of the intersection of the lines \(x+y=5\) and \(x−y=1\)?

solutions.explanation: Adding the 2 equations gives \(2x=6\), so \(x=3\). The y-coordinate is 2.
solutions.title: Add to eliminate y

solutions.explanation:
The first equation gives \(y=5-x\). Substituting this into the second equation leaves only \(x\):
\[
x-(5-x)=1,\qquad 2x=6.
\]
Thus \(x=3\), and then \(y=5-3=2\). The intersection is \((3,2)\), so its \(x\)-coordinate is \(3\).
solutions.title: Substitute y from the first equation
